newsitem.title: UK: Transco says storage tender heavily oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Transco says storage tender heavily oversubscribed.

text.p: Transco, the pipeline and storage arm of BG Plc, said on Friday that its annual gas storage tender was heavily oversubscribed.
The tender for the 1997/98 storage year, which starts on May 1, attracted 28 bidders compared with 19 last year, Transco said in a statement.
And reflecting increased competition in the U.K. gas market, Transco reported that the value of bookings by customers other than British Gas was 90 percent above last year's total.
Capacity at the Hornsea storage site, which is able to release gas into the transportation system at short notice, was two and a half times oversubscribed, the statement said.

Transco at present controls all gas storage in the U.K. Its main facility is Rough, a mostly depleted gas field off the Yorkshire coast which holds 2.8 billion cubic metres of gas, or 82 percent of Transco's total capacity.
It also has high pressure storage in salt cavities at Seal Sands on Teesside and five liquefied natural gas (LNG) sites around the country.

But the Hornsea salt cavities in East Yorkshire, with a capacity of 189 million cubic metres and a direct link to the National Transmission System (NTS), are the real prize for shippers struggling to deal with daily balancing under the Network Code.
"Rough is a very useful thing to have access to but it's no use on peak days," said a gas trader for an electricity utility.

On the basis of accepted tenders, the clearing price for Hornsea capacity will be at least 3.709 pence per kilowatt hour (p/kwh) for peak day demand, more than three times last year's price of 1.208 p/kwh.

The highest bid was heard to have been 13 p/kwh, and disappointed tenderers claimed that some players entered bids way off market levels knowing that the clearing price would be set at the lowest accepted bid.

"I think the person who puts in the highest price should get filled at that price, otherwise you're just encouraging gaming bids that they don't really have any intention of paying," said one shipper who was left empty handed in the tender.

Industry watchers believe that a lack of gas storage in the U.K. -- which meets only five percent of annual gas consumption compared to 20 percent in the United States -- will be a key driver of spot price volatility, particularly as competition in domestic sector hots up.
Independent supplier United Gas, a subsidiary of U.S. Utilicorp United Inc, is set to become the first to break Transco's storage monopoly by developing its own salt cavity facility in Cheshire.
The company expects the 11.3 million cubic metre site, which will be able to release gas into the transmission system in less than an hour, to be in use by late 1999.
